problem: Reach many more students than a campus lecture hall.
title: Stanford professors offer an introductory AI course free online
context: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence was a standard Stanford course taught on campus.
decision_made: Offer the course free online worldwide from 10 October to 18 December 2011.
action_taken: Registration opened in the summer of 2011; Norvig was Google's research director at the time.
observed_outcome: More than 58,000 students had registered by 15 August 2011, and a later report cited 160,000. Thrun then decided to stop teaching by lecture at Stanford and focus on a venture-funded initiative, Udacity.
lessons: Open access can reveal very large unmet demand and can reshape a career or institution.
limitations: The 160,000 figure appeared only in a Wikipedia-based source. Completion rates and learning outcomes were not checked here.

claims.claim_text: Thrun and Norvig offered Stanford's introductory AI course free online in autumn 2011.
More than 58,000 students from around the world registered for the free course by 15 August 2011.
